Phase 13 verification: the user correctly pointed out Estonia produces pasta domestically (Tartu Mill) and grows its own wheat -- confirmed true (Tartu Mill's own product listing gives spaghetti ingredients as durum wheat flour and water; Wikipedia confirms Tartu Mill mills wheat/rye flour, semolina, pasta and feed). But the wheat Estonia grows in large surplus is common/soft wheat (bread and feed wheat), not the durum wheat pasta requires -- per PIKK.ee's agricultural extension guide, 'Estonia grows soft wheat varieties because durum needs a drier, more continental climate' than Estonia has, and per ERR/Novaator (2024), durum is only being trialled experimentally by a single farm (Põlgaste, two growing seasons as of the article), explicitly framed as an uncertain experiment dependent on finding a buyer -- not a tracked commercial crop. So pasta-MAKING is genuinely domestic (confirms the user's point), but it runs on imported durum wheat/semolina, the same way a country can roast imported coffee or process imported cocoa domestically without being self-sufficient in the raw crop. This replaces the earlier, unverified per-PM20 0%-durum-production claim (PM20 does not track durum separately) with sourced confirmation that pasta's raw-material self-sufficiency really is ~0%, so 156.2% remains a valid upper bound.
